answers.answer: Shuffle Factory cards and randomly select players + 1 face-down for the board; return the rest to the box without looking. Put one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories. Randomly choose one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘number of players + 1’; ‘one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories’; ‘one structure bonus tile’; ‘The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.’

answers.answer: At setup, place the character at home; two workers on the two land-adjoined territories adjoining home; four mechs over the Faction Mat abilities; six stars by the faction emblem; six technology cubes in the Player Mat green boxes marked with a black square; four structures in their matching Player Mat boxes; four recruits on its bottom-row circular spaces; the remaining six workers on its Produce red rectangles; and the action token beside the Player Mat. Leave the Faction Mat one-time recruit spaces empty. The Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; the Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins, and two objective cards.
answers.evidence: Setup, items 3–4: ‘Use the Faction Mat to set starting power and combat-card draw’; ‘Use the Player Mat to set starting popularity, coins and objectives (two objective cards)’; the setup piece table lists the starting positions.

answers.answer: You must move the token to a different section, but may take neither action (a dead turn), either action, or both. If taking both, take the top before the bottom; you cannot return to the top afterward. Rusviet may repeat a section, including its Factory card. Top-row gains may pay bottom-row costs. Costs are all exposed red boxes and must be paid in full before the action; benefits are exposed green boxes and may be taken as much or as little as desired. Exact bottom-row resource costs and coin benefits depend on the Player Mat and upgrades.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘different section’; ‘first pay the full cost’; ‘choose as much or as little’; ‘You may use top-row gains to pay the bottom-row cost’; ‘bottom first is not allowed’; ‘Rusviet may repeat a section.’

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls the territory and all its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; you keep those abilities even without control, except a Mill cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory. You may pay action costs with resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: ‘An enemy worker alone on your structure’s territory controls it and all its resources’; ‘Enemy units do not gain your structure’s abilities’; ‘Pay costs using resources from any territories you currently control, even to act elsewhere.’

answers.answer: No. On the normal Move, you may move up to two different units one adjacent territory each; you cannot use both selections to move the same unit twice. Mechs can carry any number of your workers (never your character); all units can carry resources. A transported worker's carried movement does not count as its own, so it may subsequently move itself, or may move onto a mech and be carried by that mech's later move.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: ‘move up to two different units’; ‘cannot use both selections to move the same unit twice’; ‘Only mechs may also carry any number of your workers’; ‘Being carried does not count as the worker’s own movement.’

answers.answer: A character or mech entering a territory with only enemy workers stops and cannot move again that turn. Those workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources; lose one popularity per worker, down to zero. Insufficient popularity does not prevent retreat. It is not combat. The mech's own workers cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: ‘Your character/mech entering enemy workers only stops’; workers ‘immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources’; ‘Lose one popularity per worker, down to zero’; ‘A worker cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.’

answers.answer: After the attacker finishes moving the other units, resolve all combat before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: ‘Finish moving the other units, then resolve all combats before the bottom-row action; attacker chooses multiple-combat order’; a worker cannot independently move ‘into or out of’ territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card before upgrades. If the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck; if both deck and discard pile are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources, same or different, or one popularity, before upgrades. Traded resources go on a controlled territory with at least one worker. You cannot Trade for resources if all your workers are at home. A built Monument adds one popularity to Bolster; a built Armory adds one power to Trade.
answers.evidence: Bolster: ‘Pay $1, gain two power OR one combat card’; empty deck reshuffle and both-empty rule. Trade: ‘Pay $1’; resources go to ‘a controlled territory containing at least one worker’; ‘cannot Trade for resources if all your workers are at home.’

answers.answer: Produce first requires paying every exposed Produce cost in full, including power, popularity and/or coins, before production. Then choose up to two different controlled territories; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that same territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and are put in the producing village after payment. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Exposing new costs affects future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce steps: ‘Pay every exposed Produce cost … in full before production’; ‘Each worker … may produce one’; ‘Take new workers from the Player Mat left to right, after payment’; ‘You may decline’; new costs affect ‘future Produce actions.’

answers.answer: Upgrade costs oil: move any technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost; solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded. Deploy costs metal: put a chosen mech on a controlled territory containing your worker, never a lake. Its uncovered ability applies from then on to your character and every mech, not workers. Even after all upgrades, mechs, structures, and recruits are completed, you may still pay for the bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: ‘Upgrade — oil’; ‘Deploy — metal’; ‘The uncovered ability applies from now on to your character and every mech, not workers’; completed actions may still be paid for coins and recruit bonuses.

answers.answer: Build costs wood. Place a structure on a controlled territory with your worker; only one structure total may be on a territory, including opponents' structures. The Factory is allowed; lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot be moved or destroyed. A Mill supplies a bonus Produce territory and produces as one worker only while you control its territory; an enemy unit there removes control, so the Mill cannot produce. A Mine is your personal tunnel for all your unit movement, including Factory Move, even while enemy-controlled; it does not grant opponents its ability.
answers.evidence: Build: ‘controlled territory with your worker’; ‘Only one structure total’; ‘Structures cannot be moved or destroyed’; Mill works ‘only while controlled’; Mine is ‘personal tunnel … even when enemy-controlled.’

answers.answer: Take a recruit from any bottom-row section of your Player Mat and put it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on your Faction Mat. Immediately gain the chosen one-time bonus: two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is determined by the Player Mat circle uncovered where the recruit was removed: Upgrade gives one power, Deploy one coin, Build one popularity, Enlist one combat card. For a triggered bonus, resolve active player first, then left neighbor, then right neighbor; stop if a sixth star ends the game. In two-player play, the opponent triggers it once, not twice.
answers.evidence: Enlist: recruit from ‘any bottom-row section’; one-time bonus list. Ongoing recruits: bonus is the ‘circle uncovered where you removed the recruit’; resolve ‘active player first, then left, then right’; two-player opponent triggers ‘once, not twice.’

answers.answer: Each player secretly chooses dial power from 0 to the smaller of seven and current power. They may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech, even with zero dial power; Rusviet People's Army adds one additional card total if any workers are present. Workers alone never fight. If both combatants have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously and add dial and card values; attacker wins ties. Each player, winner and loser alike, deducts their dial power from the power track and discards every played card face-up. Card values do not deduct extra track power.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–3: dial ‘0 to the smaller of seven and your current power’; cards per participating character/mech; ability order attacker then defender; ‘attacker wins ties’; both players deduct dial and discard cards.

answers.answer: The winner controls the territory and resources and places a combat star if eligible (normally at most two combat stars; Saxony has no usual limit within six available). All losing characters, mechs, and workers retreat to their home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy allows eligible units and carried workers to retreat to adjacent lakes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, even workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none. Polania Camaraderie exempts the specified post-combat aggressor worker retreat loss. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
answers.evidence: Combat step 4 covers territory, stars, retreats and resources; step 5 covers attacker popularity loss and loser card draw.

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter only if the character remains in the territory; discard the token and draw the card before a following bottom action. If the character loses contested entry, it retreats and the encounter token stays. All resources, workers, mechs, and structures gained go to the encounter territory. Pay no additional normal action costs and receive no additional mat benefits, including no ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Encounters: ‘After the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there’; on lost contested entry ‘the token stays’; gains go to ‘the encounter territory’; ‘Pay no additional normal action costs’ or mat benefits/recruit bonuses.

answers.answer: Every player's character, on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if necessary), looks at available Factory cards, chooses one, and returns the rest. Each player gets at most one permanent card; later visits cannot exchange it. The card acts as a fifth action section, with optional top then bottom under the usual no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception). Factory actions give no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories within that Move action, or three for a character/mech with Speed; Mine access and ordinary movement/stop restrictions apply.
answers.evidence: Factory: ‘Every player’s character’ on ‘its first finish of a Move action’; ‘one permanent card’; fifth section; no mat/recruit bonuses; bottom action moves one unit two territories, or three with Speed.

answers.answer: Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective; you may wait but must meet all requirements at the moment of reveal. Place its star and put both objective cards on the bottom of the deck. Normally only one objective star is allowed. Saxony retains the other card after the first objective and can score both.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements: ‘Only on your own turn’; ‘meet all requirements at the moment of reveal’; put ‘both objective cards on the bottom’; Saxony retains the other card and can score both.

answers.answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony's exception. Stars are permanent if power or popularity later drops, and another player's stars never block a goal. Play ends immediately when someone places their sixth star.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end: lists each achievement; ‘A placed star is permanent’; ‘Other players’ stars never block a goal’; ‘sixth star immediately ends play.’

answers.answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, first collect the primary benefit, coins, and the active player's ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. Resolve neighbor power/popularity recruit stars in this order: finish the active action, active player first, left neighbor, right neighbor, checking for a sixth star at each step; if an earlier player places the sixth star, later recruit stars or bonuses do not resolve. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement and return initiating units to their origin territories; do not resolve another combat.
answers.evidence: Sixth-star sequence: collect ‘primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing that star’; neighbor order active, left, right; pending battle movement is undone and no other combat resolves.

answers.answer: At 10 popularity, each star is $4, each controlled territory $3, and each complete pair of controlled resources $2. Thus 5 stars = $20; four ordinary territories plus the Factory count as seven territories, scoring $21; 13 resources make six complete pairs, scoring $12. These add $53 to held coins. The selected structure bonus is also scored even if enemies control the player's structure territories. Tiebreakers, in order: workers + mechs + structures (not character), power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune table/example gives at 10 popularity five stars, four ordinary territories plus Factory, and 13 resources = ‘$20 + $21 + $12 = $53’; structure bonus applies even if enemies control those territories; tiebreak sequence is listed.
